statement: A model m consists of u in R with 0 <= u and a total function r: R -> R such that for every z in R there exists delta in R with |delta| <= u and r(z)=z(1+delta). T(A) denotes finite ordered binary trees generated by leaf(a), a in A, and node(L,R), L,R in T(A); there is no empty tree. The exact product tree replaces each leaf (a,b) by ab. The rounded product tree replaces each leaf (a,b) by r(ab). Both preserve tree shape. The perturbation target asserts that corresponding resulting leaf values p,q satisfy |q-p| <= u|p|. The two equality targets identify roundedProductTerm(m,a,b) with model multiplication and model multiplication with r(ab). The rounded dot product subsequently reduces the rounded product tree by applying r to each internal-node sum. No supplied target bounds the error of that final scalar reduction.

targets.name: Research.BinaryTreeReduction.roundedProductTerm.eq_1
targets.statement: For every model m and all x,y in R, roundedProductTerm(m,x,y)=Model.mul(m,x,y). A model m consists of u in R with 0 <= u and a total function r: R -> R such that for every z in R there exists delta in R with |delta| <= u and r(z)=z(1+delta). This identifies the operation applied to every leaf pair by roundedProductTree, and hence the multiplication stage of roundedDotProduct. Combined with the definition of Model.mul, both sides equal r(xy); the statement does not assert equality to 1.

targets.name: Research.BinaryTreeReduction.roundedProductTree_isPerturbation
targets.statement: For every model m and every t in T(R x R), IsPerturbation(u,exactProductTree(t),roundedProductTree(m,t)). A model m consists of u in R with 0 <= u and a total function r: R -> R such that for every z in R there exists delta in R with |delta| <= u and r(z)=z(1+delta). T(A) denotes finite ordered binary trees generated by leaf(a), a in A, and node(L,R), L,R in T(A); there is no empty tree. For any real bound b, IsPerturbation(b,A,B) is the inductively generated relation: leaf(x) is related to leaf(y) when |y-x| <= b|x|, and node(L,R) is related to node(L_prime,R_prime) when the corresponding children are related with the same b. Thus the target asserts identical ordered tree shape and, at each leaf originally labelled (a,b), |r(ab)-ab| <= u|ab|. The tree shape, number of leaves, and real leaf pairs are arbitrary. It compares the actual exact and rounded product constructions before any of the additions used by roundedDotProduct.

targets.name: Research.FloatingPoint.Model.mul.eq_1
targets.statement: For every model m and all a,b in R, Model.mul(m,a,b)=m.round(ab)=r(ab), where ab is the ordinary real product. A model m consists of u in R with 0 <= u and a total function r: R -> R such that for every z in R there exists delta in R with |delta| <= u and r(z)=z(1+delta). Together with roundedProductTerm.eq_1, this identifies the computation at each leaf of roundedProductTree, also used in roundedDotProduct. It does not assert equality to 1.

constructions.name: Research.BinaryTreeReduction.exactProductTree
constructions.description: A function T(R x R) -> T(R). It sends leaf((a,b)) to leaf(ab), using ordinary real multiplication, and node(L,R) to node(exactProductTree(L),exactProductTree(R)). It preserves ordered tree shape and returns a tree of individual products. It performs no arithmetic between different leaves. This is the first tree in the perturbation target.

constructions.name: Research.BinaryTreeReduction.roundedDotProduct
constructions.description: For every model m, a function T(R x R) -> R defined by roundedDotProduct(m,t)=roundedSum(m,roundedProductTree(m,t)). Here roundedSum(m,leaf(v))=v and roundedSum(m,node(L,R))=r(roundedSum(m,L)+roundedSum(m,R)). Equivalently, roundedDotProduct(m,leaf((a,b)))=r(ab), and roundedDotProduct(m,node(L,R))=r(roundedDotProduct(m,L)+roundedDotProduct(m,R)). It rounds each leaf product once and each internal-node sum once, following the given tree grouping. There is no empty-input case or additional rounding of the final scalar beyond these operations. The supplied targets describe its product stage but give no error bound for this final scalar.

constructions.name: Research.BinaryTreeReduction.roundedProductTree
constructions.description: For every model m, a function T(R x R) -> T(R) that maps each leaf pair (a,b) to roundedProductTerm(m,a,b)=Model.mul(m,a,b)=r(ab). Thus leaf((a,b)) maps to leaf(r(ab)), and node(L,R) maps to node(roundedProductTree(m,L),roundedProductTree(m,R)). Ordered shape is preserved, with no arithmetic at internal nodes. This is the second tree in the perturbation target, with bound m.u, and the input to roundedSum in roundedDotProduct.

assumptions: A model m consists of u in R with 0 <= u and a total function r: R -> R such that for every z in R there exists delta in R with |delta| <= u and r(z)=z(1+delta).

T(A) denotes finite ordered binary trees generated by leaf(a), a in A, and node(L,R), L,R in T(A); there is no empty tree. Input pair labels range over all of R x R; resulting scalar labels and outputs lie in R.
All target quantifiers are universal over the displayed models, real operands, and input trees. Model properties are packaged in the model; there are no additional target hypotheses.
The error witness delta may depend on z. There is no supplied upper bound on u, no assumption u < 1, and no specified floating-point format or restriction on real operands.
There is no balancing requirement, depth bound, prescribed leaf count, or nonzero-leaf requirement.

IsPerturbation is defined for every real bound b without a separate nonnegativity premise. Its leaf rule is |y-x| <= b|x| and its node rule relates corresponding children using the same bound. The target uses b=u, which is nonnegative by the model condition.
